newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JAN 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JAN 2.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The national economy ministry is planning on a redistribution of European Community funds, as part of efforts to aid better absorption, within the first quarter of the New Year. Deputy Economy Minister Christos Pahtas will begin a round of talks with ministries on the subject next week.

--The government's bill on cutting loose the central bank from state intervention will be submitted to Parliament in February. The bill will change the planning framework for monetary and exchange policies, in line with Maastricht treaty conditions, including the establishment of a monetary policy committee.
--The government is considering the merger of the Bank of Crete with the Hellenic Industrial Development Bank (ETBA) in case offers for the state-run bank are not satisfactory.

--The New Year will mean changes to the housing market as the full deregulation of rentals of homes and business premises will be complete by mid-year. Agreements contracted between the two sides will carry the most weight, with state intervention trimmed back to the bare minium.

--The national economy ministry is considering expanding the denationalisation of state-owned firms and organisations in cooperation with the development ministry. A report is expected to be handed to minister Yannos Papandoniou in the next few days, which will be followed by meetings with the competent ministries to choose the enterprises.

--Greece's telecoms organisation OTE will once again open the bidding for increases in charges and tariffs at state utlities (DEKO). OTE plans to increase the standard subscription rate by 12.12 percent, call charges by 12.75 percent per unit, the price of phonecards by 200 drachmas and increase tariffs on calls to Balkan countries. Increases are also expected in post office charges and rail, Olympic Airways and urban public transport services.

--Structural changes are needed in the economy to allow an improvement in comptetitiveness and productivity and the speedier de-escalation of inflation. As governor of the Bank of Greece Lucas Papademos has stressed, the improvement in the mixture of policies is not necessary only to reduce inflation but is of crucial importance to achieving sustained economic development and stability in exchange parities.

--Industrial production was up by 0.7 percent in the first eight months of the year but this small achievement appears to have been scuttled by December's 25-day farmers' blockade of road and rail links. The blockade cost industry 56 billion drachmas, or 0.7 percent of estimated value of production for 1996, according to the Federation of Greek Industries (SEB).
--The government is asking for social support for its measures and is planning immediate talks with social groups, including business for early in the new year.
--The taxation of state titles will harm mutual funds as their relatively high returns were based on investments in state titles and placement with derivatives.
